result.summary: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. No coverage gap. EXECUTED (MIX_ENV=test, one mix at a time under the mixlock): after mix compile --force (498 files, no warning) the four files together, seed 4242: 83 passed in 57.9 s; mix format --check-formatted over the fixture, the 3 new test files, enforced_audit_actions_test and identity_gh2547_audit_test: exit 0; after my one test edit, the four files again with LOG_LEVEL=error: 83 passed in 54.3 s (so no LOG_LEVEL dependence, the 2e-a T-L6 lesson does not recur) and format exit 0. Nine own mutants (A..I), compiled in memory only: 9 of 9 killed. The T-S15 order deviation from design 8.2 is JUDGED CORRECT: with the design's order (sync queued first, rebind behind it) the sync commits before the rebind and a before-lock read and an after-lock read agree, so it cannot kill the C-3 mutant; the shipped test queues the rebind first and keeps the design order as a control; my mutant A (roles read before lock A) is killed by exactly that test.

changes_made.change: strengthened 'dedup is tenant-scoped': tenant B now holds an audit entry with EXACTLY the resource id tenant A's sync would write (binding.pending_scope, user_a.id:SYNC_ROLE_A); the test asserts A still writes its own entry (deduped 0, trace id of the sync) and B still holds only its foreign entry
changes_made.why: the original only showed that B had no entry after A's sync, which a dedup that read another schema or ignored the schema would also satisfy; a cross-tenant entry with the same id is the discriminating fixture
changes_made.verified: 83 passed under LOG_LEVEL=error after the edit; mix format --check-formatted exit 0

findings.title: Tenant-scope of the dedup was asserted too weakly (fixed by this validator)
findings.detail: See changes_made. No mutant that is expressible without a second schema in the query was found for the prefix, so the fix is pinned by the fixture, not by a measured kill.

findings.title: Own-tenant ids in scope_delta: read isolation is asserted, not mutation-measured
findings.detail: The test 'a snapshot of one tenant never reads another tenant's rows' and the 55-node test with a second tenant's same-role group assert no foreign id. I did not apply a mutant that widens the snapshot read across schemas (the reads take the prefix per query, no single anchor); the cap and count are measured (mutant G).

findings.title: Held-lock helpers keep the shared 700 ms per-phase deadline
findings.detail: T-S15 and T-S15c use Letflow.LockOrderHelpers.wait_for_blocked/2, whose deadline can only produce a false failure on a badly overloaded host, never a false pass. The lock is held in a separate Task transaction with a 15 s bounded receive and released in on_exit; queue order is read from pg_locks (blockers/1), no sleeps. The sync's own lock_timeout is 2 s and the release happens right after both workers are parked.

findings.title: TS-1 pinned as current behaviour
findings.detail: T-S12 asserts {:ok, original_user} for a swallowed failure and states it; a future failure variant changes that assertion on purpose. Acceptable for this slice (REVIEWER step-12 TS-1 asked only for the pin).

findings.title: Not killable branch: non-raising {:error, _} of the suppression audit write
findings.detail: Audit.insert_entry/3 raises rather than returns an error tuple for a valid schema and normalised trace id, so write_once/6's error branch is unreachable from a test; the raising variant is covered by T-S1b and T-S12. Agreed with TEST-DESIGNER.

fixture_and_flake_review.isolation: Every database file is async: false and builds its own committed tenants through EnforcedWritersFixture (tenant!/seeded_tenant!, on_exit teardown; the run end sweep printed clean DROP SCHEMA/DELETE lines). Fault triggers and functions are dropped in after; the renamed-schema helper restores the name in after; the lenient key is restored in with_lenient_key. The registry file is async: true and reads only lib/ and the AST: no DB, no Application env, no global state. No test depends on another test.
fixture_and_flake_review.formatting: mix format --check-formatted exit 0 on all six touched test/support files, before and after my edit.
fixture_and_flake_review.log_lesson: Refutations on whole captured logs are only on unique claim values (uuid-based external id, e-mail, display name, a constant realm string); id, group name and role refutations are applied to the entry payload dumps, not to a log. Group and user names (rsg-g-N, rsg-user-N) cannot collide with hex ids in a payload. T-S12c's two refutes name strings that exist in lib/letflow/identity.ex (the Logger.error text 'transaction raised' and the exception module), so they are not vacuous.
fixture_and_flake_review.flake: Lock tests use a real held lock A with queue order read from pg_locks and bounded waits (F-3). Audit entry ordering: RSG.entries orders by a utc_datetime_usec timestamp, so the two-entry assertions in 'the delta lists only changed roles' are not second-boundary sensitive (#2729 shape absent: no api_tokens.last_used_at, no wall-clock read). No per-entity INSERT list is compared verbatim anywhere in the new files (PR #2850 lesson: grep for INSERT finds nothing).
fixture_and_flake_review.ci_environment: I recompiled with mix compile --force before the baseline (no stale _build dependence); no test-only config key beyond :scope_mode_lenient_for_tests which is set via with_lenient_key; files are read with project-relative paths (docs/roles.md, lib/...) the same way the existing scan tests do; LOG_LEVEL=error run: 83 passed; runtime of the 83 tests 54 to 58 s on this host.
